title: Effectiveness of a Generate–Verify–Repair Pipeline with Batfish for LLM‑Generated Vendor CLI Configurations
abstract: We report a preregistered paired experiment (cnsms2026-001-gvr-batfish-prereg-v1) that evaluated a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline using a single sampled initial LLM candidate per task (shared_initial_candidate semantics), a deterministic network validator, and at most one automated LLM repair call. Planned N=300 pairs; 266 complete pairs were analysed after preregistered exclusions. Baseline pass-rate = 260/266 (97.744%); guarded (final GVR) pass-rate = 265/266 (99.624%). The preregistered primary decision procedure was the exact two‑sided McNemar test (discordants n10=5, n01=0) which produced p = 0.0625 and therefore did not reject at α = 0.05. A paired bootstrap percentile interval (B=10,000, seed=1729), reported as a supplementary descriptive estimator, is [0.0037593984962406013, 0.03759398496240601]. Repair was invoked for 6 episodes; median repair iterations per task = 0. Provider/stage accounting records hosted_model_call_event_count = 306, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 272, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 34, shared_initial_generation = 300, repair = 6. Per‑episode latency was not archived and could not be evaluated. All execution and analysis artifacts (validator traces, model responses, reconciliation manifests) are archived per the preregistration (manifest SHA‑256: 46a223492f760950b3d06f475129ce21e52e296c4c2a1e09df3ccd50bec9f891) to enable reproducibility and audit.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are being explored for NetOps tasks such as intent→CLI translation, zero‑touch configuration synthesis, and automated maintenance workflows [1]. Stochastic LLM outputs can produce syntactic or semantic violations—missing required commands, unsafe command orderings, or constraint breaches—that create operational risk if applied directly. A common mitigation pattern is generate–verify–repair (GVR): produce a candidate with an LLM, deterministically validate it with a domain verifier (e.g., Batfish‑style analysis), and apply bounded repairs if the verifier fails. Prior work proposes components and prototypes for GVR in code and NetOps domains, but preregistered paired evaluations that archive validator traces and quantify verifier‑triggered repair benefit on reproducible NetOps task banks remain limited. This study addresses that gap by evaluating the incremental effect of a single validator‑triggered repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics on a preregistered intent→CLI task bank.
sections.related_work: Recent surveys and benchmarks document growing interest in LLMs for network operations and recurring failure modes that motivate grounding and verifier integration [1,2]. NetConfEval‑style evaluations study translation quality for vendor CLI fragments, showing that vendor dialects and sequencing constraints remain persistent failure points for unconstrained generation [1]. Generate–verify–repair and related generate‑and‑validate architectures are proposed to combine stochastic generation with deterministic oracles and bounded repair steps, with demonstrations in code generation and regulated document tasks [3]. Deterministic network verifiers (Batfish and header‑space analyses) provide concrete acceptance criteria for reachability and ordering checks but have finite rule coverage and expressiveness tradeoffs that shape outcomes when used as GVR oracles [4]. Our work contributes a preregistered, artifact‑archived paired test (shared_initial_candidate semantics) that isolates the effect of a verifier‑triggered bounded repair on verifier pass rates.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand: The experiment followed preregistration cnsms2026-001-gvr-batfish-prereg-v1 (manifest SHA‑256: 46a223492f760950b3d06f475129ce21e52e296c4c2a1e09df3ccd50bec9f891). The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline under shared_initial_candidate semantics: a single sampled initial model candidate per task is used to evaluate both baseline (initial candidate scored by the deterministic validator) and guarded (if that same candidate fails, at most one automated repair call is permitted, followed by re‑scoring). The preregistered primary decision rule is the exact two‑sided McNemar test at α = 0.05; we explicitly report this as the confirmatory inferential procedure. A paired bootstrap percentile confidence interval (B=10,000, seed=1729) is reported as a supplementary descriptive interval estimator and is not used to overturn the preregistered hypothesis test.
sections.results: Execution accounting and missingness: The preregistered plan targeted 300 tasks (600 episodes). Execution manifest and deterministic reconciliation artifacts record planned_episode_count = 600, completed_episode_count = 532, failed_episode_count = 68, and complete_pair_count = 266 after applying the preregistered missingness rule 'complete_pair_primary' that excludes both‑arm provider/infrastructure failures. The deterministic_reconciliation.json artifact (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json; SHA‑256: 32ea4be9caac88b78993caafec4ac323b8b822f1b6813e0e3747f3144e7a4490) archives these reconciled counts. Provider/stage accounting (from reconciliation) shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 306, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 272, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 34, shared_initial_generation = 300, and repair = 6. Explicitly, 'shared_initial_generation' denotes the single sampled initial candidate produced once per task and reused for both baseline and guarded evaluations under shared_initial_candidate semantics; 'repair' counts the additional LLM calls invoked only when that shared initial candidate failed the deterministic validator.
sections.discussion: Primary inferential outcome: For the 266 analysed pairs the paired contingency table is n11 = 260, n10 = 5 (guarded success only), n01 = 0 (baseline success only), n00 = 1. The preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test on the discordants (total = 5) produced p = 0.0625 and therefore did not reject at α = 0.05; this is the preregistered confirmatory decision. A paired bootstrap percentile CI (B=10,000, seed=1729) for the paired difference is [0.0037593984962406013, 0.03759398496240601] and is reported as a descriptive supplement. Repair yield and operational scalars: repair was invoked in 6 episodes; median repair iterations per task across analysed pairs = 0. Derived number‑needed‑to‑treat (NNT) for this run is ≈ 53 (1 / 0.01879699248), a descriptive scalar reflecting the high baseline pass rate. Limitations that affect interpretation include high baseline first‑pass accuracy (few discordants and limited power), finite validator rule coverage (semantic violations outside the deterministic_netops_validator_v5 battery are unmeasured), runtime nondeterminism (model configuration recorded temperature = null and no deterministic sampling seed archived), and absence of per‑episode timing (the preregistered latency estimand could not be evaluated).
sections.conclusion: Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics the GVR pipeline (gpt‑5‑mini initial candidate + deterministic validator + ≤1 automated repair) produced a small absolute increase in deterministic‑validator pass rate (0.0188) on the analysed task bank. The preregistered exact McNemar test did not reject at α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). Supplementary paired bootstrap resampling yields a narrow descriptive CI excluding zero for the observed sample, but this CI is reported only as a descriptive measure and not as the preregistered decision. Repair calls were rare (6/300) and the median per‑task repair count = 0. All execution and analysis artifacts (raw responses, validator traces, provider call accounting, and reconciliation manifests) are archived to permit reanalysis and targeted audits.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure (concise): Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini"). Orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Preregistration: cnsms2026-001-gvr-batfish-prereg-v1 (manifest SHA‑256: 46a223492f760950b3d06f475129ce21e52e296c4c2a1e09df3ccd50bec9f891). Initial master‑prompt immutable reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human role and autonomy boundary: prior to the autonomy lock a human Research Director selected the topic family and approved pre‑lock infrastructure development; after the autonomy lock the registered pipeline autonomously performed literature selection, preregistration, experimental execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, AI peer review simulation, and revision. Provider/stage accounting (archived in deterministic_reconciliation.json) records hosted_model_call_event_count = 306, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 272, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 34, shared_initial_generation = 300, repair = 6. Shared_initial_candidate semantics was executed as preregistered: one sampled initial candidate per task was produced (shared_initial_generation) and reused for baseline scoring and for the guarded pipeline; additional model calls labeled as 'repair' were invoked only when that shared initial candidate failed. Nondeterminism disclosure: execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null (unset) and no deterministic sampling seed; nondeterministic sampling of model outputs cannot be excluded for recorded provider calls. Execution and analysis artifacts, logs, and hash manifests are archived in the evidence bundle referenced by the preregistration.
limitations: Shared_initial_candidate semantics: both arms used the same single sampled initial candidate per preregistration; the estimand measures validator‑triggered repair benefit for that fixed initial sample and does not evaluate independent first‑pass generations or constrained first‑pass prompting strategies.

Missingness and sample reduction: planned N = 300 pairs; after infrastructure/provider exclusions 266 pairs were complete and 34 both‑arm episodes were excluded per the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule (see deterministic_reconciliation.json; SHA‑256: 32ea4be9caac88b78993caafec4ac323b8b822f1b6813e0e3747f3144e7a4490), reducing effective sample size and precision.
Small discordant counts: primary inference used exact McNemar with few discordants (n10 = 5, n01 = 0); conclusions are sensitive to inferential choice and limited power for small absolute effects.
Validator coverage: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces a finite set of syntactic/semantic/reachability rules; semantic violations outside its coverage are possible and unmeasured.
Runtime nondeterminism and sampling: execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null and no deterministic seed; nondeterministic sampling cannot be excluded for recorded model calls.
H2 latency not evaluated: per‑episode end‑to‑end latency was not present in archived per‑task artifacts and therefore the preregistered latency bound (median ≤ 60 s) could not be assessed.

External validity: task corpus derives from public NetConfEval‑style examples and a seeded synthetic generator limited to two vendor‑dialect clusters; results do not imply universal benefit across other vendors, larger topologies, or production deployments.
